text.p: Hundreds of land-mine victims, monks, activists and officials gathered in nationwide ceremonies on Monday to commemorate National Mine Awareness Day in Cambodia, one of the most heavily mined countries in the world.

Ieng Mouly, information minister and chairman of the Cambodian Mine Action Centre (CMAC), told a rally in Phnom Penh that anti-personnel land-mines pose the single biggest threat to the nation's development.
"Land-mines are the largest obstacle to national development and reconstruction, and have a serious impact on the quality of life of many people," he said.
Ieng Mouly said war-scarred Cambodia had 2,600 mined areas covering 3,600 square kilometres. Only about 34 square kilometres have been cleared.
Those areas alone contained 61,000 anti-personnel mines, 600 anti-tank mines and 384,000 pieces of unexploded ordnance.
One in 250 people in Cambodia is an amputee, the highest rate in the world, he said.
On Tuesday, delegates from Cambodia are scheduled to attend the Fourth International Conference on Land-mines in Maputo, Mozambique, to help lobby for a global ban on mines.
